natural.statement: Let E be a type equipped with a normed additive commutative group structure and with a normed vector space structure over the scalar field of real numbers. Let Q be a subset of E, let μ be a real number, and let f be a function from E to the real numbers. The proposition StrongConvexC1On Q μ f is the one-constructor predicate whose data are exactly the following: Q is convex over the real numbers; μ is strictly positive; f is continuously differentiable of order 1 on Q; and f satisfies the first-order lower bound that, for every point x of Q and every point y of Q, f(x) + (fderivWithin ℝ f Q x)(y − x) + (μ / 2) · ‖y − x‖² ≤ f(y). Here fderivWithin ℝ f Q x is the derivative of f within Q at x, used as a continuous linear map from E to the real numbers and evaluated at the vector y − x, and ‖·‖ is the norm of the given normed additive commutative group structure on E. Equivalently, any proof of StrongConvexC1On Q μ f yields each of these four pieces of data, and these four pieces of data together construct StrongConvexC1On Q μ f.
